question: A 500-billion-kg black hole lasts about 14 billion years. Lifetime goes with mass cubed. What mass lasts 14 years, in thousand tonnes?
answer: 500 billion kg / 1,000 = 500 million kg = 500 thousand tonnes.
move: When an effect goes with a cube, a vast change needs only a modest step.
trap: Dividing the mass by a billion, as if lifetime followed mass.
hint: Ask which number, cubed, gives the factor by which the lifetime shrinks.
steps: 14 billion years / 14 years = a lifetime 1 billion times shorter.
The cube root of 1 billion is 1,000, so the mass is 1,000 times smaller.
500 billion kg / 1,000 = 500 million kg = 500 thousand tonnes.
reference: Page, Particle emission rates from a black hole: Massless particles from an uncharged, nonrotating hole, Physical Review D, 1976
